description: Phase 6 evidence: modular character composition from Pixel Assets, resolved from persisted cosmetic keys, with safe fallback verified against a real configuration.
proof: A character composes from pedestal + character + wearable + aura + held item, resolved from persisted cosmetic keys, at every density, with no application knowledge inside the display.

contractExtension.reason: CharacterConfig has an equipped pedestal slot and an equipped aura slot. A pedestal is under the character and an aura surrounds it; forcing either into wearable would have meant an anchor that lied about what it attached to.
contractExtension.newValidationRule: grid-larger-than-host — a composed asset shares its host reference grid.

o19GroundOwnership.change: The grass moved from the character asset to the pedestal asset. It did not move a pixel: same row, same tufts, same colours.
o19GroundOwnership.evidence: CharacterConfig.pedestal is an equipped slot with its own identifier, so the ground is chosen and can change. A ground welded into the character would double up or need hiding.
o19GroundOwnership.sparklesReason: No equipped slot selects them and they are specific to this character. Moving them would have been change for its own sake.

o20NestedComposition.model: One host plus a flat list of parts, one level deep. A part is an asset, and an asset has no slot list, so recursion and cycles are impossible.
o20NestedComposition.enforcement: A test asserts no reference asset has a parts or children property; declaring a slot twice paints it once.

registry.rule: Persisted keys are the authority. Nothing renames a key, invents one, or asks a scholar to re-equip.

form.status: supported, all resolve to the base figure
form.note: 16 forms exist in the catalogue; one character is authored

deferredWithEvidence: 15 of 16 forms exist as 90x90 PNGs; migrating them is artwork, not architecture.
AURA_PRESETS contains only none; the reference ember aura proves the mechanism, the real aura art does not exist.
RELIC_OPTIONS contains only the unequipped relic; no scholar can equip a held item yet.

realConfigurationFallback.conclusion: A valid, populated character. Not a blank card.

unchanged: CharacterRenderer and all 11 of its other consumers
surfaceMigration.dataFlow: characterConfig -> registry -> asset ids -> composition -> SylfCharacterContent; every arrow one-way

boundaryChanges.change: Display-path allowlist widened from content$ to content(/|$)
boundaryChanges.why: Phase 6 reaches the asset contract one level down. Reaching the content is the point of an integration surface.

boundaryChanges.change: Dual-vocabulary list now names two modules: the adapter and the dev review panel
boundaryChanges.why: The panel must show the same resolution a scholar would get, so it cannot be handed a hand-made composition. Written as an exact list so widening it requires editing the test.

boundaryChanges.change: Added: display layer may not import character-traits, shop, locker or asset-manifest
boundaryChanges.why: The reverse direction, which is what keeps application knowledge out of the display.

boundaryChanges.change: Added: content layer may not import the cosmetic registry
boundaryChanges.why: If a content module imported it, the content layer would have learned what a cosmetic key is.

boundaryChanges.change: Added: nothing outside app/dev may import the dev surface
boundaryChanges.why: The dev route is 404 in production; this stops anything shipping from pulling it in.

findings: Ambience and ground are genuinely different and Phase 5 grouping them was a simplification. Ground is equipped; ambience is character-specific. O19 was one question that turned out to be two with different answers.
The kind vocabulary was the right size at three until real slots demanded more. The extension cost one union member, one validator constant and two anchors.

A registry with three distinguishable outcomes beats one with two: collapsing unequipped into unknown would have made aura none - the default for every scholar - raise a notice on almost every dashboard load.

openDecisions.O19: Resolved for ground, still open for ambience.
openDecisions.O21: New: authoring the remaining fifteen forms as pixel assets. Architecture accepts them; artwork does not exist.
openDecisions.O22: New and genuinely undecided: whether form variants are separate assets, states of one asset, or a base plus part swap. Evidence does not exist because the artwork does not.
openDecisions.O23: New: migrating the remaining ten CharacterRenderer consumers, each on its own evidence.
openDecisions.O24: New: the aura and relic catalogues are effectively empty while live configurations already carry keys nothing defines. Worth surfacing to whoever owns them.

limits: Fifteen of sixteen form keys map to one authored figure, so the migration is proven for the mechanism rather than for the artwork.
No scholar can currently equip a held item or an aura, because the Shop offers no such keys. The held path is driven by a persisted identifier but not by a real equipped scholar.
Only the dashboard surface was migrated, so the composition path is exercised in one production context.
